message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically late winter to early spring). A male will approach a receptive female, often following her scent and vocalizing loudly. Once she signals readiness—usually by emitting a low growl or a soft roar—the male will mount her from behind. The actual copulation lasts only a few minutes, but the male may stay close afterward to guard the female and ensure he is the father of any offspring. After mating, the female will give birth after a gestation period of about 110 days, usually giving birth to a litter of 1–4 cubs.
